title: Order of operations
examples: When do I use the order of operations rules?
Does the order of operations change if I use PEMDAS instead of BIDMAS?
How do I know which operation to do first?

explain.say: Today we learn the order of operations. This tells us the right way to solve math problems. We use an order to keep answers correct.

items: Find the correct way to solve math
Use an order to keep answers correct

explain.say: Some people use PEMDAS. P stands for Parentheses. E stands for Exponents. M stands for Multiplication. D stands for Division. We always start with brackets first.

draw.text: P $ ightarrow$ E $ ightarrow$ M $ ightarrow$ D

explain.say: Next we do any exponents. Then we do multiplication and division. These two steps are done from left to right. Remember that rule.
If you see brackets, always solve what is inside those brackets first. This is the most important step to remember today.

items: This is the most important step

explain.say: Let us try one example together. Calculate two brackets plus three times four. This is two brackets plus three times four.

faq.a: BIDMAS stands for Brackets, Indices, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. It is another way to remember the order.
asks: What does the letters stand for?
What is the order of the letters?

faq.q: Do I always do exponents before multiplication?
faq.a: Yes, exponents come before multiplication. They are part of the index step in BIDMAS. You must handle them before multiplying.
asks: When do I do the powers?

faq.q: What if there are only brackets and addition?
faq.a: If you only have brackets and addition, you solve inside the brackets first. Then you do the addition outside.
asks: What if I only have brackets?

faq.q: Does the order change if I use PEMDAS?
faq.a: No, PEMDAS and BIDMAS teach the same order of operations. They are just different sets of letters for the same rules.
asks: Are PEMDAS and BIDMAS the same?
Do I have to use one specific name?

faq.q: If I have division and multiplication, which one do I do first?
faq.a: You must work from left to right. Whichever operation appears first when reading left to right gets done first.

facts: The order of operations ensures everyone gets the same answer.
Brackets always tell you which calculation to do first.
Multiplication and division have the same priority level.
When dividing or multiplying, you always work from the left side to the right side.

quiz.why: You must multiply four by two first, which is eight. Then you add ten to eight, getting eighteen. Finally, you subtract six from eighteen to get twelve.

wrong.0: This answer suggests you did the subtraction first, which breaks the correct order of operations.
wrong.2: This answer suggests you added ten and four first, which is incorrect because multiplication has a higher priority than addition.
wrong.3: This answer suggests you only did the multiplication and addition, forgetting to subtract the final number.

quiz.why: First, you solve inside the brackets, which is five minus two, giving three. Next, you multiply three by three, which is nine. Finally, you add one to get ten.

wrong.1: This answer suggests you added three and one first, ignoring the multiplication step that must happen before the final addition.
wrong.2: This answer suggests you multiplied three by three and then added five, which incorrectly uses the number five twice.
wrong.3: This answer suggests you only solved the brackets and stopped, forgetting the rest of the calculation.

quiz.say: What is the result of 12 $ ext{divided by}$ 3 $ imes$ 2?
quiz.why: Since division and multiplication are on the same level, you work left to right. Twelve divided by three is four. Then four multiplied by two is eight.

wrong.0: This answer suggests you added the numbers together before dividing, which is not part of the order of operations.
wrong.1: This answer suggests you multiplied all three numbers together without following the correct sequence.
wrong.3: This answer suggests you did the multiplication first, which is wrong because you must work from the left side to the right side.
